## 1) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Wrap returned SQL fragments in parentheses so top-level OR cannot bleed into caller predicates

Affected:
- packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:72-80
- packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:105-107
- packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:171-174
- packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:204-207

Explanation:
The org and team auth conditions are returned as a bare top-level `(A) OR (B)`. The single `eventTypeId` filter is also a bare `(...) OR (...)`.

`getBaseConditions` only adds parentheses when it combines auth and filter conditions. When there are no filters, it returns `authConditions` as-is. The same applies to callers of `getAuthorizationConditions()` or `getFilterConditions()`.

Callers will likely interpolate this into a larger query, for example `WHERE ${base} AND "createdAt" >= ${start}`. That produces `(A) OR (B) AND created...`. Because `AND` binds tighter than `OR`, this evaluates as `A OR (B AND created...)`. Rows matching `A` then skip every extra predicate the caller added, such as a date range or status filter.

With the Prisma object API, each `where` input was naturally scoped, so this is a regression in composability. It can return data outside the requested filters, and is a potential authorization leak if callers add further restrictions.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
// Make every public fragment self-contained
async getBaseConditions(): Promise<Prisma.Sql> {
  const authConditions = await this.getAuthorizationConditions();
  const filterConditions = await this.getFilterConditions();
  return filterConditions
    ? Prisma.sql`((${authConditions}) AND (${filterConditions}))`
    : Prisma.sql`(${authConditions})`;
}
// and in the builders: return Prisma.sql`(${acc}) OR (${condition})` wrapped, e.g.
return Prisma.sql`(${conditions.reduce(...)} )`;
~~~

## 2) Severity: LOW | Type: Maintainability
Title: Remove unreachable branches in getBaseConditions

Affected:
- packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:72-80

Explanation:
`getAuthorizationConditions()` always returns a non-null `Prisma.Sql` object, which is always truthy. As a result, the `else if (filterConditions)` branch can never run, and neither can the final `NOTHING_CONDITION` branch.

The dead code is misleading. It suggests that filter conditions alone could act as the base condition when authorization is missing, which would be a security hazard if it were ever reachable.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
const authConditions = await this.getAuthorizationConditions();
const filterConditions = await this.getFilterConditions();
return filterConditions
  ? Prisma.sql`((${authConditions}) AND (${filterConditions}))`
  : Prisma.sql`(${authConditions})`;
~~~

## 3) Severity: LOW | Type: Implementation
Title: Public `findMany` removed without visible migration of callers

Affected:
- packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:68-81

Explanation:
`findMany` was a public method and has been replaced by `getBaseConditions`, which has a different contract: it returns raw SQL instead of rows. Any existing callers, such as tRPC insights routers, would break at compile time. Callers that rely on `findManyArgs.where` merging would also lose behavior.

This diff does not show call-site updates. Verify that no callers remain outside these two files.

Proposed fix:
~~~text
grep for `insightsBookingService.findMany` / `.findMany(` on InsightsBookingService instances and migrate them to $queryRaw with getBaseConditions(), or keep a compatibility wrapper.
~~~

## 4) Severity: LOW | Type: Test
Title: Caching tests deleted without replacement

Affected:
- packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:426-435

Explanation:
The "Caching" describe block was removed entirely. However, the caching logic (`cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions`) still exists and was retyped. It is no longer covered by any test.

A trivial adaptation would keep the coverage: call the method twice and assert the same `Prisma.Sql` instance or an equal value. Ideally, also assert that the membership and team repositories are queried only once.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
it("should cache authorization conditions", async () => {
  const c1 = await service.getAuthorizationConditions();
  const c2 = await service.getAuthorizationConditions();
  expect(c2).toBe(c1);
});
~~~

## 5) Severity: LOW | Type: Maintainability
Title: Loosened constructor type hides invalid option combinations

Affected:
- packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:29-34
- packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:58

Explanation:
`InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` makes `teamId` optional for every scope. This means `{ scope: "team" }` without a `teamId` now type-checks.

The constructor presumably validates the options with the zod schema (that code is not shown in the diff). If so, invalid input silently falls back to `options = null`, and the service returns `NOTHING_CONDITION` (empty results) instead of failing at compile time. That makes misuse hard to diagnose.

Prefer keeping the discriminated union type, or a discriminated public type, at the constructor boundary.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
export type InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions =
  | { scope: "user" | "org"; userId: number; orgId: number }
  | { scope: "team"; userId: number; orgId: number; teamId: number };
~~~
